summary: Rare ephemeral-worker hotloop causing interleaved 5xx on low-traffic tenant
description: Issue summary: BrightNote AI (dedicated tenant) reported intermittent 5xx responses on streaming chat routes during a three-hour window on 2026-03-12 evening. Impact: degraded streaming sessions and user-visible failed tokens for ~120 requests. Environment: prod-us-east, dedicated pool, small sustained concurrency (~2-4 long-lived streams). Observed behavior: 5xxs are interleaved (not a continuous wave) and correlate with ephemeral-worker CPU surge and very short-lived runtime restarts, but only for this tenant and only when traffic is low.
customer_impact: Customer saw ~0.6% error rate spike on streaming endpoints across a three-hour window; a handful of user sessions experienced dropped streams and reconnect loops. Customer reported immediate business impact for a subset of paying users during evening hours. They requested root cause and mitigation; account-level SLA at risk for repeated incidents.
steps_to_reproduce: Observed in prod: query streaming.chat.start with a single short prompt and keep streams open for ~60s; repeat with 2-3 concurrent small sessions
Reproduced locally in staging by enabling ephemeral-proxy debug flags and lowering keepalive to 20s; rate of 503s increased when an accept-queue drain coincided with prefetch cancellation
Test harness used: loadgen script (internal) that emulates BrightNote traffic pattern (3x long-lived small-payload streams)
logs: [2026-03-12T20:11:03Z] runtime-ephemeral-42 CPU 97% hotloop detected: poll() -> prefetch_cancel -> retry() -> backoff(0ms)
[2026-03-12T20:11:04Z] apigw-178 502 upstream reset: grpc: upstream terminated unexpectedly
[2026-03-12T20:12:12Z] runtime-ephemeral-42 watchdog: restarting worker due to live-loop (reason=hotloop-detected)
investigation_notes: Initial triage (Support): validated error spike for tenant BrightNote AI in us-east between 20:05-23:15 UTC; spike is small but customer-visible.

SRE triage: CPU profiles show a tight spin between two code paths in the runtime: prefetch cancellation and keepalive handling. Hotloop occurs when a cancellation and an accept-queue re-entrant callback race.
Correlated metrics: ephemeral worker CPU, short-lived process restarts, accept_queue_depth spikes, and apigw 502/503 increments align within seconds of each other.
Hypothesis 1: a scheduler/ephemeral-proxy timing regression introduced a reentrant callback leading to a busy-wait in certain low-concurrency workflows (reproducible when keepalive < 30s).
Hypothesis 2: tenant-specific prefetch settings cause a path that bypasses usual backoff, amplifying the hotloop on low traffic where long-lived streams are present.
Staging reproduction: toggling prefetch off for the tenant eliminated hotloop; reproducer shows accept_queue oscillation is the triggering condition.
Related: linked to previous ticket SUP-412987 which had a keepalive drift fix; rolling window of changes likely exposed a race in the runtime (see PR 4892).
mitigations_applied: Immediate: Support applied account-level mitigation by disabling request prefetch for BrightNote AI (temporary) — reduced 5xxs to baseline.
Operational: SRE added an ephemeral-proxy rate limiter and bumped accept-queue threshold for the affected host pool to reduce transient overflow.
Follow-up workaround: for any dedicated tenant seeing similar symptoms, we recommend toggling prefetch to "off" and increasing keepalive threshold to >= 45s while patch is applied.

resolution: Partial mitigation: tenant prefetch disabled to stop immediate errors. Permanent fix: runtime patch v1.4.7 will include a guarded cancellation path and backoff to prevent busy-wait; scheduled rollout to prod canary on 2026-03-14, global rollout pending validation. Customer notified and workaround documented.
resolution_notes: Hotfix details: PR #4892 contains the guarded cancellation + exponential backoff change; avoids tight retry loops when accept_queue oscillates.
Canary rollout plan: 10% pool for 2 hours -> monitor CPU and 5xx telemetry -> 50% -> full rollout. Abort criteria: >0.2% increase in 5xx or CPU anomaly on non-related tenants.

Post-incident follow-up: add automated regression test in staging that simulates low-concurrency long-lived streams with prefetch enabled; add alert on ephemeral-worker spin metrics and small-tenant 5xx elevation.
Customer follow-up: Provide BrightNote AI with postmortem summary and recommended tenant config defaults (prefetch=off for now; keepalive>=45s).
